title: hook texts: the save door's literal ctx.text check misses ctx.text?.('k') and ctx.text!('k'), so an undeclared text key passes save
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

Filing gate: **(b) a defect measured during a card's development** — found by the #34575 card thread's dev (PR #35510, os-dev-report 7009580967), outside that card's scope.

## What happens
- `HookSchema.texts` TSDoc promises: "A key the hook's source asks for literally that `texts` does not declare is refused at save".
- The save-time literal check (`hook-refusal-codes`: `TEXT_CALL` / `hookTextKeysAskedIn`) only recognises the call shape `ctx.text('k')`.
- So `ctx.text('undeclared_key')` is refused at save, but `await ctx.text?.('undeclared_key')` and `ctx.text!('undeclared_key')` pass `HookSchema.safeParse`. The runtime still refuses the key, so the author learns about it only when the hook runs.
- PR #35510 declares `HookContext.text` as optional (as #35197 asks). Under strict TypeScript authors will reach for `?.(`, so the hole gets hit more often after it lands.
- Possibly the same family: the action half shares the key reader (not measured).

## Ask
- The literal reader also accepts `?.(` and `!(` call shapes (`ctx.text?.('k')`, `ctx.text!('k')`, and their `await` forms), with pins for each shape, on hooks and — if measured to share the reader — actions.
- ⛔ Not a new rule; this is making an existing declared refusal hold on every call shape it names.

## Dedup
Searched issues for `hookTextKeysAskedIn`, `TEXT_CALL`, `ctx.text optional`: only #34575 (the source card).

## Reader
The seat that takes `area:build` authoring-rule cards. Suggested grade: p2 (declared-but-unenforced save refusal, reach grows with #35510).
